patients.summary: Administrative assistant with childhood rheumatic fever and rheumatic mitral stenosis, unfollowed for years, who joins in 2020 on a thiazide. Cardiology finds severe mitral stenosis with heart failure in 2022 and paroxysmal AF on Holter (warfarin), then pulmonary hypertension in 2024; after her last practice visit in July 2024 she has an ED visit and admission for decompensated heart failure in 2026 and a balloon valvotomy, known to the practice only through late records and her messages.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer her primary care here; her old office is closing its adult panel. Medicaid, card on file. Says she has a heart valve problem from rheumatic fever as a kid and takes a water pill and potassium. New patient slot booked 9/22 at 9:00. Release signed for her former primary care office; records requested by fax.

orders.reason: rheumatic mitral valve disease, no follow-up in years

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
40-year-old woman new to the practice, transferring from another primary care office.

HPI: Had rheumatic fever as a child. Was told around high school that one of her heart valves (mitral) was narrowed from it. Saw a heart doctor a few times back then, nothing for many years since. During her last pregnancy in 2017 she got short of breath and puffy; the OB team put her on a diuretic and told her to cut salt. Her prior PCP kept her on HCTZ 25 with potassium afterward. Today she feels fine. Works full time as an administrative assistant, climbs the stairs at work without stopping. No chest pain, palpitations, orthopnea, leg swelling, fainting.

PMH: rheumatic fever in childhood, rheumatic mitral valve disease.
PSH: tonsillectomy at 8.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FH: mother had rheumatic fever. Father has type 2 diabetes. A maternal uncle had an ischemic stroke at 65.
SH: never smoker, does not drink, no drug use. Administrative assistant.

Exam: well appearing, NAD. BP 116/74. Neck: no JVD. Heart: regular rhythm; low apical diastolic murmur, otherwise normal sounds. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Ext: no edema. Skin intact.

A/P:
1. Rheumatic heart disease, mitral valve: known since adolescence, never re-imaged as an adult that she knows of. She has no symptoms on the thiazide. Recommended she get back in with cardiology for an echo and baseline; referral placed. She is agreeable though busy with work.
2. Diuretic: continue HCTZ 25 and KCl 20. CMP today.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, lipids, A1c (father diabetic), TSH; one-time HIV and hep C screens, consented. Screening mammogram ordered. Pap due per her history, will do at the physical in spring. Flu shot next month, nurse visit.
4. Prior records requested.

Return for a physical in about 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jessenia, all of your blood work from last week looks good. Kidney function, sodium and potassium are normal on the water pill. Blood counts, sugar (A1c), thyroid and cholesterol are all in a healthy range. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Please keep the cardiology appointment on your list when they call you.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received 22 pages by fax from patient's former primary care office (2016 to 2020). Summary for chart:
- Problem list: rheumatic heart disease / mitral valve disease, history of rheumatic fever.
- Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily and potassium chloride ER 20 mEq daily since 2017.
- Pap smear 2018: negative for intraepithelial lesion.
- Basic metabolic panels 2018 and 2019 within normal limits.
- No cardiology notes in the packet.
Allergies: NKDA.
Scanned to media. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal influenza vaccine. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given. Tolerated well, waited 15 minutes, left in good condition.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. No prior studies for comparison. Breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications in either breast. Skin and nipples unremarkable.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Screening mammogram negative, BI-RADS 1. Letter mailed to patient. Repeat in 1 to 2 years.

documents.title: Referral follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Cardiology office reports they mailed a letter and left two voicemails, no appointment made. Called pt: she says work has been hectic and she feels fine, will call them herself. Gave her the scheduling number again.

reports.text: Specimen: ThinPrep cervical cytology. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Feeling well. Working, mostly from the office again. Has not seen cardiology yet, says she will call this spring. No exertional symptoms, no swelling, no palpitations.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily. NKDA.
PHQ-9: 2.
Exam: BP and vitals as charted, looks well. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular with the same soft low-pitched apical diastolic murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses bilaterally. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions; Pap/HPV collected. Ext without edema.

Plan:
- Pap with HPV collected today.
- Tdap today, last one she remembers was in pregnancy, not documented.
- BMP and CBC for the diuretic.
- COVID vaccine: eligible soon, she plans to get it at her pharmacy.
- Encouraged the cardiology visit again. She understands the valve should be looked at.
Next routine visit in 6 months.

documents.title: Your Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap test was normal and the HPV test was negative, so the next one is not due for 5 years. Potassium, kidney tests and blood counts were normal too.

documents.title: covid shots
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just letting you know I got both of my covid vaccines at the pharmacy, April 6 and April 27, Pfizer. Arm was sore and I was tired one day after the second. I have the card if you need a picture.

documents.title: RE: covid shots
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thank you! Both doses are added to your record. No need to send the card.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: E-refill request for hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and potassium chloride ER 20 mEq. BMP in March normal. Approved 90 days with 3 refills per protocol.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine check. Says she has been doing well. Walks to the bus and up two flights at work, no trouble. No palpitations, no swelling, no chest pain. Taking HCTZ and potassium daily, no missed doses. Never got to cardiology; the referral from last year lapsed and she would rather wait.
O: Vitals as charted. Regular rhythm, low apical diastolic murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P: Rheumatic mitral valve disease, asymptomatic on a thiazide. I again recommended an echo through cardiology. She declines for now; we closed the old referral and she will tell us right away if she gets short of breath, swollen or notices racing heartbeats, and we will refer again. Continue current meds. Flu shot next month. Physical in March.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine given, 0.5 mL IM right deltoid, lot recorded. Denies fever or illness today. No issues after observation.

documents.title: booster
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got my booster last Tuesday the 14th at the pharmacy, same kind as before.

documents.title: RE: booster
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Got it, your booster is on your record now. Happy holidays!
